title: Model tiering storyboard and SLA mapping
content:
Purpose: capture a concrete end-to-end storyboard for graceful degradation when capacity or region constraints occur, and map each step to SLA impact, telemetry signals, and rollback actions. This is intentionally operational (play-by-play) rather than theoretical: teams should be able to walk this doc during oncall and planning.

High-level goals:
- Keep customer-visible latency and throughput predictable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Prefer quality-preserving fallbacks (model-family substitutions, quantized variants) over outright failures.
- Make control-plane decisions auditable and reversible (clear change points + runbook hooks).
- Provide per-tenant/route SLA mapping so we can tone degradation by business priority.

Assumptions and context:
- Serving mesh exposes: routeId, tenant_id, client-sla-tier (gold/silver/beta), region_hint.
- Model variants available: full-precision-large, fp16-medium, q4_0-fast, distilled-slim.
- Capacity signals: GPU-util, queue-length, request tail-latency (p99), KV-cache-hit-rate, node-availability.
- Control plane can push route-level policy updates within ~30s; rollback path is automated and manual.

Key terms (quick):
- Tiered-model: ordered set of model variants from high-quality to high-throughput.
- Local-exhaust: node-level action when local pool cannot accept requests.
- Regional-spill: redirecting requests to sibling region within latency budget.
- Soft-degrade: change that preserves response semantics (model variant swap, reduced max-tokens).
- Hard-degrade: returning HTTP 503/429 or dropping non-critical requests.

Architecture components referenced:
- Ingress router (latency-aware routing, weight knobs)
- Control plane (policy store, audit log, validator)
- Variant catalog (compatibility matrix by tokenizer/kv-format)
- Per-tenant quota/priority engine
- Telemetry pipeline (real-time SLO engine -> alerting and policy triggers)

Storyboard: request flow under increasing pressure
1) Normal: route->local-pool->preferred-variant (full-precision-large). SLA mapping: p50/p95 within goal; no action.
2) Early pressure (queue-length rising, p99 rising slowly): control plane suggests local soft-degrade hints: enable q4_0-fast as warm-standby for this route. Action: increment warm-warmup weight to 5% for new requests. SLA impact: possible minor quality delta for 5% of requests. Telemetry: newness rollout metrics and quality-checks (prompt set comparisons).
3) Moderate pressure (p99>target for 30s, gpu-util>85%): routing switches to blended tiering: route-level policy moves to 30% q4_0-fast, 70% fp16-medium. Also reduce max_tokens by 10% for non-critical routes. SLA mapping: increased latency consistency, measured quality delta on eval set. Rollback: policy store record with timestamp; automatic revert if p99 back under threshold for 2 min.
4) Local-exhaust (node failures reduce pool): ingress will mark local pool degraded and attempt regional-spill to sibling region within latency SLA (if RTT budget allows). If regional-spill selected: requests gain added network latency (SLA billing and telemetry note). Fallback order: use sibling region fp16-medium variants before q4_0-fast to preserve quality. Rollback: automatic when node_count>=min_pool for 3m.
5) Severe/global pressure (regional capacity exhausted): policy escalates to conservative hard-degrades on non-SLA-critical tenants: return 429 for beta clients, maintain gold routes by switching gold to distilled-slim but with guaranteed throughput. Provide graceful degradation banner in API response metadata (x-redwood-degrade-level). SLA mapping: defined per-tenant tiers — gold retains p95 target but with lower max_tokens; silver keeps p99 within increased latency window; beta best-effort.
6) Emergency (control-plane lost or network partition): ingress falls back to local hard policy: circuit-breaker enforced per-route; cached responses for repeat prompts where possible. Oncall: follow emergency runbook.

Policy decision matrix (condensed):
- Trigger: GPU util>85% or p99>target for 30s => action: blend to next variant, annotate change in audit log.
- Trigger: Node down causing local capacity < 50% => action: regional-spill if RTT increase < 80ms and sibling capacity > 30%; else escalate to per-tenant shedding.
- Trigger: Regional capacity < 20% for >2m => action: enforce hard-degrade on beta, preserve gold via model slimming + reserve slots.

Per-tenant SLA mapping (example):
- gold: keep p95 <= target, support region-failover, max token reduction <= 20%, no hard-429 for business routes.
- silver: soft-degrades allowed (variant swap, 30% blended q4), may experience higher p99 latency window.
- beta: best-effort, eligible for 429 under severe pressure, eligible for regional spill without priority.

Control plane roles and auditability:
- Policy changes are small JSON patches (routePolicyDelta) with metadata: reason, triggered_by, metric_snapshot, revert_criteria.
- All automated changes are stamped with a policyRunId and stored; human-triggered changes require brief rationale before commit in UI (or can be done via API with an approver flag).
- Revertability: every change must carry a target_revert_condition (time or metric-based). Reverts are executed by policy reconciler and emit a 'revert' event.

Operational runbook (short) — for SRE/oncall
- Step 0: triage p99 spike -> check telemetry, examine affected routes and top 10 prompt sets.
- Step 1: confirm model-variant compatibility for affected routes (variant catalog quick check).
- Step 2: if automated policy not engaged, issue soft-degrade: increase q4 weight to 20% for non-gold routes.
- Step 3: if local pool reports node failures, enable regional spill to specified sibling region via control plane UI or API.
- Step 4: if regional capacity count < threshold, enact manual tenant-shedding policy targeting non-critical tenants.
- Post-incident: create incident note with policyRunIds and revert events for audit.

Telemetry and quality monitoring:
- Required metrics: per-route p50/p95/p99, model-fidelity-sample (periodic BLEU/ROUGE-like signals or embedding-similarity to reference), tail-latency histogram, regional-rtthist, kv-cache-hit-rate.
- Quality guardrails: sample N requests per minute (stratified by tenant, route) for automated A/B quality tests when variant swaps exceed 10% traffic. If quality delta exceeds threshold, immediate rollback.

API/Client considerations:
- Clients receive degrade hints in response headers (x-redwood-degrade-level, x-redwood-variant) and should be recommended to gracefully degrade UX (shorten completion window, reduce followups).
- Documented SDK feature: fallbackCallback that can surface degrade-level to app for mitigation (e.g., fall back to cached answer).

Rollback checklist (quick):
- Identify policyRunId(s) from telemetry -> fetch policy diffs.
- If quality delta > threshold, trigger immediate revert via control-plane revert endpoint.
- If revert fails or control-plane unreachable, temporary mitigate by blocking traffic to affected pool via router-level hold.
- Notify affected customers with estimated ETA and cause.

Experimentation and gradual rollout plan:
- Canary: roll soft-degrade to 1% of traffic for 15m; run fidelity comparison job.
- Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 2–6 hours, stop if fidelity regression > 2% on tracked metrics.
- Per-tenant beta experiments to tune per-route thresholds.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we expose per-route degrade policy to customers via the Console? (pros: transparency; cons: more complexity/support surface)
- How aggressive should cross-region spill be vs. preserving model-fidelity (latency vs. quality tradeoff)? Need customer research on acceptable RTT bump.
- Should we add client-side SDK heuristics that proactively batch or drop retries when degrade hints are present?

Appendix: quick links and references
- Variant compatibility matrix: https://confluence.redwoodinternal/variant-catalog
- Control-plane policy API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-controlplane/blob/main/api.md
- Incident ticket template: JIRA-INFRA-987

Notes to self: test this storyboard in chaos-week — inject node drain + qps spike and verify automatic revert works. Capture real degrade headers and surface them in Console incident timeline.
